source.title: Internal Cross-layer Gradients for Extending Homogeneity to Heterogeneity in Federated Learning
source.authors: Yun-Hin Chan; Rui Zhou; Running Zhao; Zhihan Jiang; E. Ngai

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity with CKA across federated client models and reports how it varies with data and model heterogeneity. This is a conceptual test of partial alignment and its dependence on setting, not a scale sweep.
record.gate_note: The relevant findings are the study's own CKA measurements of client-model representations. Accuracy tables, gradient-distribution analyses, and t-SNE visualizations are not recorded as CKA similarity results. The paper also reports CKA increases after InCo Aggregation, but those are deliberately produced by a method designed to increase similarity and are not evidence of spontaneous convergence with scale.
record.test_reason: The CKA case study compares federated client models. These are not independently trained: FedAvg repeatedly averages their shared parameters, and hetero clients are sub-networks split from one server model. Their similarity is produced by joint optimisation, not convergence of independent models, so it bears on no version. CKA is used as a bias diagnostic to motivate InCo Aggregation, which deliberately raises similarity. Li et al. 2015 is cited only as a neuron-alignment method.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The case study finds that client accuracy correlates with layer CKA, that shallow layers are more similar than deep ones, and that smoother gradients go with higher similarity. InCo Aggregation uses normalised cross-layer gradients to raise deep-layer similarity and improves heterogeneous FL accuracy at no extra communication cost. The record omits the gradient-smoothness observation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear CKA to compare representations of local client models in federated-learning settings; it does not reproduce the original studies' methods or test their scale claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported CKA varies with layer depth and federated data/model heterogeneity. The study uses linear CKA and the same test-data batch for its comparisons.

fits_no_version.finding: Among FedAvg-aggregated client models, linear CKA is lower in deeper layers and falls with non-IID data and architecture heterogeneity. It correlates positively with client accuracy (Fig 1, 17, 18).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representational similarity among jointly trained (federated) models declines with depth and with client data or architecture heterogeneity, and tracks accuracy.

record.problems: The CKA results are presented as plots without tabulated numeric values or reported uncertainty. The case study uses small federated scales: ten clients in the stated settings. The study uses linear CKA only and focuses on image classification and federated client models.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant CKA measurement rows omitted. Accuracy results and gradient-distribution results were excluded because they are not direct measurements of representation similarity.

untested.parts: No independently trained models and no scale or capability sweep of alignment.
No comparison of independent seeds' features or subspaces. The seed check in G.4 concerns gradient distributions only.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
Only linear CKA on one test batch. No variation of the metric, its settings or the evaluation inputs.
No independent models, so neither the degree of convergence nor its causes are assessed.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 and V7 links rest on treating federated clients as independent models; they are not, since averaging couples them. The InCo-induced CKA gains (Fig 10, 19) are deliberately produced and also bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No scaling sweep or relationship between model size/capability and alignment of independently trained models.
Different-seed gradient distributions are discussed, but the study does not measure shared features or subspaces across seeds.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are assessed.

Uses linear CKA only; does not compare other similarity measures or metric settings, and does not test out-of-distribution evaluation inputs. It varies federated training/data and model-architecture settings.
Measures incomplete and setting-dependent similarity, but does not test whether shared data or objectives explain alignment rather than a common model of reality, nor whether alignment plateaus.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ResNet and ViT client models across IID/non-IID and homogeneous/heterogeneous federated settings
reader_labels.reason: CKA similarity changes with the reported data and architecture settings; the paper states that increasing heterogeneity lowers layer-wise similarity (R1-R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Shallow versus deep layers, especially in non-IID heterogeneous settings
reader_labels.reason: Similarity is not uniform across layers: the study reports lower CKA in deeper layers and reduced similarity as data and model heterogeneity increase (R1-R12). It does not establish the proposed causal explanation involving shared data/objectives.
